payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly have a chalk-like drawing medium or surface treatment?
node.criteria: pass: visible chalk-like marks or texture establish a chalk medium; fail: the image is clearly rendered in a non-chalk medium with no visible chalk treatment; unknown: the medium cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Assess only visible evidence that the image uses a chalk-like medium or treatment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a visibly grainy, smudged, chalk-like surface treatment across the scene, with softened sketchy outlines and textured shading.

n3: The node’s own criteria make “complete” require both supports to pass, and both saved supports do pass; the trace is valid, queried, and has no transport or dependency failure. The edited image also visibly has a chalk-like grainy, smudged treatment and drawn outlines, so the evidence does not justify changing either support to fail or treating low confidence as missing progress. The mismatch is instead that the aggregate says “yes” while the reference is “partial.” Clarify the requested-node outcome mapping so that “complete” is not automatically emitted as the aggregate’s yes when the rubric’s partial label applies, and inspect the aggregation/label conversion for this node. Preserve the separate chalk-medium and drawing-form checks and their evidence; do not weaken the completion criterion or invent additional visual requirements to force agreement.
n2: The drawing-form check is well scoped and its pass is supported: the edited image has visibly drawn outlines and a sketch-like rendering, unlike the photographic source. Do not change this support to fail or add chalk-medium criteria; that is a separate check. The mismatch is at the aggregate level: a pass here (and the separate medium check passing) is being converted to “yes,” while the reference is “partial.” This node alone cannot resolve that mapping. Preserve its visual criterion and evidence, and route the repair to the parent/aggregation logic that combines requested changes and maps completion to the rubric labels. The trace is valid and has no transport or dependency failure.
